llm.summary: This skill mostly does what it advertises, but it needs review because it can fetch and screenshot unvalidated URLs from feeds and then asks agents to read reports containing untrusted web content.

dimensions.detail: Outbound network access is expected for this purpose, but it is broad: feed URLs, search endpoints, redirects, and product links are not constrained to public HTTPS destinations, and Chromium is launched with --no-sandbox.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No hidden installer, startup hook, or package-fetching code was found; documentation lists Python and Playwright dependencies and gives an explicit Chromium install command.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill tells agents to read report.md and parse launches.json, while report.md directly embeds RSS and search-result text without labeling it as untrusted data or warning agents not to follow instructions found there.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script writes reports, JSON, and screenshots only under the user-specified output directory and does not create persistence, but it reads BRAVE_API_KEY from the environment and sends it as the Brave API authentication header when present.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The RSS, search, screenshot, scoring, and report-writing pipeline matches the stated AI launch-monitoring purpose, but custom feed URLs and feed-provided entry links are accepted without validation and then fetched or opened in Chromium.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill making broad outbound web requests and rendering feed-provided pages from the machine running the agent. Prefer trusted feed lists, use --no-screenshots for untrusted feeds, avoid running it in environments with access to internal services or cloud metadata, and treat all generated reports, JSON, screenshots, and links as untrusted web data.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Confirmed BRAVE_API_KEY flows into the Brave Search API X-Subscription-Token header. That is normal API authentication for the documented Brave integration, not credential exfiltration by itself, but it should be more explicit to users.
[LP3] expected: The skill discloses network access, screenshots, environment use, and output files, but it lacks tight permission scoping for domains, writable paths, and environment access; this contributes to review because the URL handling is broad.
[E1] expected: The Brave and DuckDuckGo network calls are expected search-enrichment behavior for the launch-monitoring purpose.
[SQP-2] expected: The documentation mentions BRAVE_API_KEY, but the CLI help and workflow do not clearly state that an ambient environment credential will be transmitted to Brave when search enrichment runs.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed material concern: arbitrary feed URLs and feed entry links are fetched or opened in Playwright without scheme, hostname, private-network, redirect, or resolved-IP validation.
[T01] unexpected: Confirmed material concern: untrusted RSS and search-result text is inserted into report.md, and the skill instructs agents to read that report without an untrusted-content boundary.
